claim: manualPagination makes the table assume data is already paginated; you must supply rowCount or pageCount (-1 for unknown), and autoResetPageIndex is disabled automatically.
quote: Setting the `manualPagination` option to `true` will tell the table instance to use the `table.getPrePaginationRowModel` row model under the hood, and it will make the table instance assume that the `data` that you pass in is already paginated.

claim: manualFiltering disables built-in filtering logic; the table uses the data you pass as-is.
quote: When `manualFiltering` is set to `true`, the table instance will not apply any filtering logic to the rows that are passed to it.

claim: manualSorting tells the table the data is already sorted and to apply no sorting itself.
quote: When manualSorting is set to true, the table will assume that the data that you provide is already sorted, and will not apply any sorting to it.

claim: manualGrouping exists but TanStack Table has no practical server-side grouping story.
quote: There are not currently many known easy ways to do server-side grouping with TanStack Table. You will need to do lots of custom cell rendering to make this work.

claim: With manualPagination + manualFiltering, pageIndex is not reset to 0 when column filters change; the user stays on page 1000 and gets empty results. Open issue.
quote: Manual Pagination doesnt reset PageIndex when Manual Column Filtering. (server-side, v8)

claim: TanStack Table V9 entered beta on 7 June 2026 with TanStack Store state, plugin-registered features, and large memory/type wins; no change to the server-side manual model.
quote: Announcing TanStack Table V9 Beta today!

claim: Official TanStack example combines react-table, react-query useInfiniteQuery and react-virtual for virtualized infinite scroll.
quote: React TanStack Table Virtualized Infinite Scrolling Example

claim: placeholderData: keepPreviousData keeps the last successful fetch visible across query-key changes and swaps seamlessly; isPlaceholderData gates the Next button.
quote: The data from the last successful fetch is available while new data is being requested, even though the query key has changed.

claim: TanStack Query v5 removed keepPreviousData and isPreviousData in favour of placeholderData and isPlaceholderData.
quote: The keepPreviousData option and isPreviousData flag have been removed as they were doing mostly the same thing as placeholderData and isPlaceholderData flag.

claim: Cursor pagination uses useInfiniteQuery with getNextPageParam returning the server's next cursor; maxPages caps retained pages.
quote: getNextPageParam and getPreviousPageParam options are available for determining if there is more data to load and the information to fetch it.

claim: SWR 2.x keepPreviousData: true keeps prior data when the key changes, the SWR equivalent of Query's keepPreviousData for paginated tables.
quote: With keepPreviousData enabled, you will still get the previous data even if you change the SWR key and the data for the new key starts loading again.

claim: AG Grid SSRM lazy-loads rows and groups; getRows request carries startRow/endRow, sortModel, filterModel, rowGroupCols, groupKeys, valueCols, pivotCols; filtering, sorting, grouping, pivoting and aggregation execute on the server.
quote: The Server-Side Row Model builds on the Infinite Row Model and in addition to lazy-loading the data as the user scrolls down, it also allows lazy-loading of grouped data with server-side grouping and aggregation.

claim: AG Grid has four row models; Client-Side and Infinite are Community, Server-Side and Viewport are Enterprise. SSRM is recommended over Infinite for Enterprise customers.
quote: Server-Side Row Model is Infinite Row Model plus more. So if you are an AG Grid Enterprise customer, you should prefer Server-Side Row Model over Infinite Row Model.

claim: IServerSideDatasource.getRows(params) responds via params.success({rowData, rowCount}) or params.fail().
quote: Grid calls `getRows` when it requires more rows as specified in the params. Params object contains callbacks for responding to the request.

claim: Infinite Row Model cannot group or aggregate; cacheBlockSize defaults to 100, maxBlocksInCache evicts LRU, blockLoadDebounceMillis suppresses fetches while scrolling, and sort/filter changes purge the cache and refetch.
quote: Aggregation and grouping are not available in infinite scrolling. This is because to do so would require the grid knowing the entire dataset, which is not possible when using the Infinite Row Model.

claim: AG Grid React cannot be server-rendered; it needs 'use client' because it depends on browser APIs.
quote: We created a client-rendered component because the `ag-grid-react` library depends on some browser-specific APIs (e.g., `window` / `document`) and can not be rendered server-side.

claim: You cannot call useQuery inside AG Grid's getRows; use useQueryClient() and queryClient.fetchQuery inside the datasource, memoise it, and include all request params in the query key.
quote: AG Grid's callbacks (like onGridReady or the getRows function in a Server-Side datasource) are not React components, so you cannot call React hooks such as useQuery inside them.

claim: GridDataSource.getRows receives filterModel, sortModel, paginationModel, start/end, groupKeys, aggregationModel; the grid handles caching (GridDataSourceCacheDefault, 5-min TTL, swappable via dataSourceCache), errors via onDataSourceError, dataSourceKeepPreviousData and dataSourceRevalidateMs polling.
quote: The Data Source supports an optional updateRow() method for updating data on the server... GridDataSourceCacheDefault has a default time to live (TTL) of 5 minutes.

claim: Server-side lazy loading requires Data Grid Pro; known rowCount gives viewport loading with skeleton rows and a 500ms request throttle, rowCount=-1/undefined gives infinite loading at scroll-end.
quote: A new page is loaded when the scroll reaches the bottom of the viewport area.

claim: Server-side aggregation is a Premium-plan feature using aggregationModel in getRows plus a getAggregatedValue() getter on GridDataSource.
quote: Pass the getter method `getAggregatedValue()` in `GridDataSource` that defines how to get the aggregated value for a parent row (including the `aggregateRow`).

claim: paginationMode="server" + rowCount + onPaginationModelChange is the manual path; rowCount going undefined during loading resets the page to zero; unknown counts use rowCount={-1} with paginationMeta.hasNextPage or estimatedRowCount.
quote: If the value `rowCount` becomes `undefined` during loading, it will reset the page to zero.

claim: The MIT Community DataGrid exposes paginationMode, sortingMode and filterMode ('client' | 'server', default 'client') and a dataSource prop of type { getRows, updateRow? }.
quote: Sorting can be processed on the server or client-side. Set it to 'server' if you would like to handle sorting on the server-side.

claim: MUI X v8 moved the Data Source into the Community (MIT) plan and added server-side aggregation, infinite scrolling and lazy loading on top of it.
quote: The Data Source now supports advanced features such as server-side aggregation, on-demand data fetching for infinite scrolling, and lazy loading.

claim: Mantine React Table exposes manualPagination and requires you to override pageCount/rowCount and manage pagination state yourself, fetching in a useEffect.
quote: Mantine React Table will assume that the `data` that is passed to the table already has had the pagination logic applied.

claim: Mantine React Table is a Mantine wrapper around TanStack Table V8; latest tagged release is v1.3.3 from October 2023.
quote: Built with Mantine V7 and TanStack Table V8

claim: createSearchParamsCache parses searchParams in a Server Component and propagates typed values down the RSC tree without prop drilling; parsers are shared with client useQueryStates.
quote: Think of it as a loader combined with a way to propagate the parsed values down the RSC tree, like Context would on the client.

claim: nuqs useQueryState with shallow:false notifies the server to re-render Server Components; throttleMs rate-limits URL writes and server requests while hook state updates instantly (default 50ms, ~340ms on Safari).
quote: the state returned by the hook is always updated instantly, to keep UI responsive. Only changes to the URL, and server requests when using `shallow: false`, are throttled.

claim: Reference implementation of TanStack Table + Next.js with server-side pagination, sorting and filtering, advanced filter menus and virtualized infinite scroll.
quote: Server-side pagination, sorting, and filtering

claim: Marking a file 'use client' pulls it and everything it imports/renders into the client bundle; React context is unavailable in Server Components.
quote: once a file is marked with "use client", all of its imports and the components it directly renders are included in the client bundle.

claim: Network responses may arrive out of order; the ignore-flag cleanup guards against it, and React recommends a framework's data fetching or TanStack Query / SWR instead of hand-rolled effects.
quote: network responses may arrive in a different order than you sent them.

claim: Without debouncing a server-side table fires a request per keystroke; you must own and coordinate search, filter and pagination state yourself and merge them into every request.
quote: you perform a request with every keystroke made in the search field.
